From: Jonathan Smith <jonathan.smith@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing ask — expected throughput & reserved slot guidance

Marcus / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're trying to finalize the pilot configuration so procurement can lock in budget. A few quick data points from our side:
- Expected steady-state: ~100 inference requests / second (avg payload)
- Peak bursts: up to 300 rps for ~5 minute windows during morning ET batch jobs
- Typical prompt length: 300 tokens in, ~250 tokens out on average
- Availability target: 99.5% for the pilot window (6 weeks)

Can you confirm what reserved slot configuration you'd recommend (GPU type + slot count) and a headline monthly committed spend? We're fine with a small committed reserve + burst credits if that materially reduces cost.

Appreciate a quick alignment this week — we have an internal procurement cutoff on July 6.

Thanks,
Jonathan Smith
Head of AI Platform | Acme Corp
jonathan.smith@acme.com


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask — expected throughput & reserved slot guidance

Jonathan —

Thanks — useful numbers. Quick first-pass mapping below (we can refine after you confirm concurrency distribution):

Option A — Cost-sensitive (mix of reserved + burst):
- Hardware: 1 x A10G-style reserved pool + autoscale burst to T4-equivalent
- Reserved slots: 4 slots -> steady-state handling for ~120 rps with batching and KV cache
- Burst: up to additional 6 burst slots for short windows
- Expected monthly committed spend (headline): ~$26k 

Option B — Latency SLO first (dedicated throughput):
- Hardware: 2 x A10G reserved slots (or equivalent) pinned for low-latency
- Reserved slots: 8 slots -> comfortable for sustained 300rps with lower batching
- Expected monthly committed spend (headline): ~$48k

Assumptions: 1) batching factor ~1.8 for your payload distribution, 2) we leverage prefix caching for repeated prompts from batch jobs, 3) quantization not applied for pilot.

I've attached a short throughput profile (acme_throughput_profile.csv) and a GPU-fit matrix (redwood_gpu_fit_matrix.xlsx) so the finance and infra teams can see the unit economics. Also linking our internal cost model here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePilot

If you want, Laura or I can fold this into a short one-pager for procurement.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment: acme_throughput_profile.csv

Laura / team —

Quick take from finance: Option A (4 reserved + burst) headline is ~$26k/mo as Marcus estimated. We could offer a pilot pricing structure: 6-week minimum term with a 10% pilot discount and up to 2000 burst credits for the pilot window.

If they want Option B (8 reserved), that's ~48k/mo; that would require a larger quarterly commitment to get to ~15% discount territory. Also flag: August looks tight for additional reserved capacity until some deals roll off.

Action items I propose:
- Offer Option A as the default pilot commercial: 6-week commit, 10% off, 2000 burst credits.
- Add clause: can move to Option B with 30 days notice and reprice at the then-current committed rate.

Attaching a quick cost deck for the internal review.

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on the finance signal, here's a recommended pilot proposal to present to Acme procurement:

- Pilot configuration: Option A (4 reserved A10G-equivalent slots + up to 6 burst slots)
- Commercial: 6-week minimum commit, headline ~$23.4k/mo after 10% pilot discount, includes 2000 burst credits for the pilot window
- Operational notes: we will enable aggressive prefix caching for the morning batch window and set burst auto-throttles at 6 slots to protect the pool
- Risk & contingency: if actual sustained peak > 250 rps for > 10 minutes, auto-fallback to queued requests and we will trigger an escalation to infra to provision temporary extra capacity (manual approval)

Please review and let me know if finance needs a small tweak to the coupon/discount language. If we're aligned, Laura can share the one-pager and I will schedule the 30-minute technical handoff with Acme for next Tues (July 6) at 10am PT.

Next steps (proposed):
- Laura: send one-pager to Jonathan and procurement by EOD tomorrow
- Ben: finalize pilot pricing terms in HubSpot and attach the DocuSign
- Karthik: hold tentative capacity for 4 reserved slots + burst before July 6; call out any outright conflicts now

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
